findings.title: TLS certificate expires in 12 days
findings.explanation: An unrenewed certificate will cause outages at expiry.

findings.title: Passive scanner data lists CVE identifiers for 104.20.30.40
findings.evidence: 1 CVE ID(s) in Shodan InternetDB (unverified), e.g. CVE-2021-41773
findings.explanation: InternetDB infers vulnerabilities from service banners seen by a crawler, which can be stale, backported-patched or wrong. VESTIGE did not test the host.
findings.recommendation: Verify the actual software version and patch status on the host (with authorisation).

findings.title: Domain registration expires in 35 days
findings.explanation: An expired or soon-to-expire domain can lapse, causing outages and exposing the name to re-registration by others.
findings.recommendation: Renew the domain and enable auto-renew; check that registrar contacts are current.

findings.title: AbuseIPDB reports abuse confidence 32% for 104.20.30.40
findings.explanation: AbuseIPDB aggregates community reports over 90 days. Shared hosting, NAT and compromised-then-cleaned hosts can inflate scores; it is not proof the owner is malicious.
findings.recommendation: Review the report categories on AbuseIPDB and check whether the host was compromised or is shared infrastructure.

findings.title: HSTS header not set on HTTPS site
findings.explanation: Without HSTS, a browser's first plain-HTTP visit can be downgraded or intercepted by a network attacker. This is a hardening gap, not an exploitable flaw by itself.
findings.recommendation: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains once all subdomains support HTTPS.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.evidence: No DNSKEY or DS record found for the zone.
findings.explanation: DNSSEC adds origin authentication to DNS answers. It is optional, and many well-run domains do not use it.
findings.recommendation: Consider DNSSEC if the registrar and DNS host support it.

findings.title: No CAA records
findings.evidence: No CAA record set at vestige-demo.example.
findings.explanation: CAA restricts which certificate authorities may issue certificates. Absence means any CA may issue.
findings.recommendation: Consider publishing CAA records naming the CAs you use.

findings.title: 1 historical hostname(s) no longer resolve
findings.explanation: These names appear in archives but returned no DNS answer when tested. They may be decommissioned; check that no dangling CNAMEs/records point to released resources. VESTIGE did not test for takeover.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the hostnames are intentionally retired.

findings.title: DMARC policy is monitoring-only (p=none)
findings.explanation: p=none asks receivers not to act on failing mail. It is a normal first step of a DMARC rollout but offers no enforcement.
findings.recommendation: If reports show legitimate mail is aligned, move to p=quarantine and then p=reject.

findings.title: No MTA-STS policy published
findings.explanation: MTA-STS lets a domain require TLS for inbound SMTP and protects against downgrade attacks. Adoption is optional.
findings.recommendation: Consider publishing MTA-STS (start in testing mode) and TLS-RPT.

findings.title: Browser hardening headers not set
findings.explanation: These headers reduce the impact of XSS, MIME sniffing and information leakage. Their absence is a defence-in-depth gap, not a vulnerability; some are irrelevant for API-only hosts.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate each header against the application's needs and add where appropriate.

findings.title: Version information disclosed in HTTP headers
findings.explanation: Version strings help attackers match known vulnerabilities, but they do not mean the software is vulnerable (it may be patched or masked).

findings.title: No security.txt published
findings.evidence: Neither /.well-known/security.txt nor /security.txt returned a text file.
findings.explanation: security.txt gives researchers a standard way to report vulnerabilities. It is optional.

limitations: FIXTURE DATA: produced from canned responses by `vestige demo`; no network requests were made.

Direct checks inspected only the root host over HTTPS. Missing headers are configuration observations, not exploitable vulnerabilities. A DNS-rebinding race between the public-address check and the request is possible in principle (see docs/SECURITY.md).
Passive subdomain sources are incomplete by nature; absence of a name is not evidence it does not exist.
Subdomain states: 'resolved' = DNS returned an address at test time; 'no_dns_answer' = no A/AAAA answer; 'wildcard_only' = answer matches a wildcard record; 'unverified' = not tested or lookup error.
Third-party reputation and exposure data are other parties' observations, not VESTIGE verdicts.
